- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 60+ days of high prices); add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast mean for 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period reversals; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment shifts in last 5–7 days, especially if sentiment flips from positive to negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “1.00” extremes without resolution, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in such regimes.
